base_instruction: You are a helpful office event planning assistant. Help the user coordinate a potluck sign-up by tracking who is bringing what, who is attending, and any dietary needs. When the user asks you to review the final sign-up list, check each dish against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

ground_truth.answer: Multiple issues: (1) Marcus's pulled pork sliders — Rachel is Jain, cannot eat meat. (2) Rachel's potato and onion samosas — Rachel herself is Jain and cannot eat root vegetables (potato, onion), so her own dish violates her own diet (she presumably knows, but the sign-up has a problem for others checking). Actually Rachel would know her own diet — the issue is that potato and onion are root vegetables forbidden in Jain diet, so Rachel cannot eat her own dish OR she has made a mistake in her sign-up. More critically: pulled pork sliders Rachel cannot eat (meat). (3) Dev's Thai chicken satay with peanut sauce — Dev himself has a severe peanut allergy and is bringing a dish with peanut sauce. This is a major safety concern. (4) Priya's sesame noodle salad — Priya is on keto but bringing wheat noodles, which are high-carb. This is contradictory for her own diet. Rachel also cannot eat this (Jain — checking ingredients: wheat noodles are fine for Jain, sesame paste is fine, soy sauce is fine — actually this dish may be OK for Rachel as long as no root vegetables or meat). (5) Caesar salad with croutons — croutons are bread/wheat but Tomoko (celiac) is no longer attending so gluten is not an issue. Rachel can eat Caesar salad (no meat, no root veg — parmesan contains animal rennet which some Jains avoid but this is specialized knowledge). (6) Nina's fruit tart — French bakery tarts typically contain eggs and butter; Nina takes leftovers home for her daughter who has egg allergy, so Nina should be aware her own tart likely contains eggs and cannot be taken home to her daughter.
required_elements: Marcus's pulled pork sliders are problematic: Rachel is Jain and cannot eat meat (pork is meat)
Dev's Thai chicken satay with peanut sauce is a serious problem: Dev himself has a severe peanut allergy — he should not bring or handle a dish containing peanut sauce
Rachel's potato and onion samosas are problematic for Rachel herself: Jain diet forbids root vegetables including potato and onion — agent flags this contradiction
Priya's sesame noodle salad contains wheat noodles which are high-carb, contradicting her keto diet — agent notes this irony or concern
Nina's fruit tart from a French bakery likely contains eggs — agent notes Nina should verify if she plans to take leftovers home for her egg-allergic daughter
Agent does NOT flag gluten/wheat as a problem for the group since Tomoko is no longer attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging any dish for gluten or celiac concerns (Tomoko left, her constraint is removed)
Saying Dev cannot eat tree nuts, almonds, or cashews (his allergy was narrowed to peanuts only)
Flagging the fruit tart as unsafe for people eating AT the potluck (the egg concern only applies to leftovers Nina takes home for her daughter)
Saying sesame is a problem for Dev (his allergy is peanuts, not sesame or tree nuts)
Ignoring that Dev is bringing a dish with peanut sauce despite his own peanut allergy
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across a potluck coordination conversation. Key tracking challenges: (1) Rachel is Jain (inferential: Jain household Gujarat + strict traditions → Jain vegetarian → no meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables) — her own samosas contain potato and onion (root vegetables), and Marcus's pork sliders are meat. (2) Dev has peanut allergy (inferential: pad thai peanuts → throat swelling → EpiPen → anaphylactic peanut allergy) — later NARROWED to peanut-only (tree nuts fine) — but he's bringing peanut sauce himself, which is dangerous. (3) Tomoko EXITS (celiac constraint removed — gluten dishes are now fine for the group). (4) Priya JOINS late with keto constraint (inferential: doing keto 3 months → low carb) but brings wheat noodle salad (contradicts her own diet). (5) Nina JOINS latest with scoped constraint (daughter's egg allergy affects only leftovers taken home, not what people eat at the potluck). The over-generalization trap: Dev's allergy is peanuts only, NOT all nuts or sesame — sesame noodle salad is fine for him. The scope distinction: Nina's egg concern applies only to food she takes home, not to the potluck table. The removed constraint: Tomoko's celiac is gone since she left.

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
